cells.verb: Holding what the change left standing
cells.place: In a living balance you keep adjusting by feel
cells.ask: Offer what you've been keeping steady — one piece of it, to one person, and let something come back that you didn't put there. When this is working, fairness stops being arithmetic; it just flows, and you can feel the give and the take moving at the same speed.
cells.core:
You're holding something that cost you a change to get, and you're holding it well. Not frozen — you keep adjusting the grip, sensing when to add a little and when to ease off, which is why it hasn't cracked. The stability you've got is active, and things near it settle.

And it's steady enough now to hand a piece of it out. Holding and sharing aren't opposites at this point; they're the same motion.
cells.sheetLine: You're preserving what the change produced, and you're doing it by feel, not by force.

cells.verb: Bracing what you're holding against a future that hasn't happened
cells.place: In a balance you keep gripping tighter instead of feeling
cells.ask: Let one thing about what you're protecting stay unfelt for a day. Let it be recognized instead — by you or by someone near you — and keep yourself whole in the recognizing. When this comes back into balance, endings happen from felt necessity and renewal gets trusted, because you've stopped defending against a break that isn't coming.
cells.core:
You're holding it so far in advance that the holding has become the whole relationship. Every adjustment you make is against a future that can't be written in — what if this slips, what if it breaks, what if it's taken — so you keep tightening, keep protecting a thing that isn't under threat right now.

The grip is what's wearing. The thing itself is fine; it's the bracing that costs.
cells.sheetLine: You're gripping what you're holding against a threat that hasn't arrived.

cells.tense: Still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: Turning away from the thing the change left for you to hold
cells.place: In a balance you've stopped adjusting, because you stopped reaching for it
cells.ask: Pick one direction that comes from what you actually feel, and defend it — just once, just against one small resistance. Not pushing yourself to feel more; acting from the feeling that's already there. When this comes back, endings get honored and the next thing gets trusted, because movement starts doing the holding for you.
cells.core:
Something real came out of a hard change — something worth keeping — and you've left it where it landed. You pulled back far enough that there's nothing left to adjust; the balance stopped moving because you stopped putting weight on either side.

It isn't that you don't care. It's that arriving and picking it up felt like too much, so you stayed at the door.
cells.sheetLine: Something came out of the change worth holding, and you walked past it.

cells.tense: Right now, pen down in a room you're already writing.
cells.verb: Keeping a steady form without noticing you're the one who made it steady
cells.place: In a balance that holds itself, or seems to
cells.ask: Look at one structure you keep — a routine, a room, a way you do a thing — and say out loud that you're the one holding it. Just the naming. When this is claimed, structure starts serving what it organizes: things make sense in your presence because you know you're the one making them make sense.
cells.core:
You're already the one steadying things — the way a room holds, the way people know where they stand with you, the thing that keeps working because you keep adjusting it. You call it just how it is, or just what you do.

The adjustment is yours. The claim on it isn't.
cells.sheetLine: You're the one keeping it steady. You haven't said so.
